beats.headline: Pink Crocs, a cat, and the end of the world
beats.text: Three in the morning, a Seattle cold snap. Carl cracks a window for a cigarette and his ex-girlfriend's show cat goes out through it and up a tree. He follows her in a leather jacket, boxer shorts and Bea's pink Crocs, and that is the only reason he is standing outside when every building on Earth comes down at once. A voice gives the terms: eighteen floors, each on a clock, and the planet back from the Borant Corporation for whoever reaches the bottom. At the foot of the stairs the achievements arrive in a wall, a Goblin Murder Dozer takes both Crocs, and Carl earns his way into Mordecai's guild hall by landing on a goblin engineer barefoot. Mordecai is an indentured guide, currently a rat, on his seventh or eighth human world, and he has one rule above all: read the description. Then Donut eats the Enhanced Pet Biscuit out of Carl's hand and gets up talking. She has the higher stats, so she takes the party, names it the Royal Court of Princess Donut, makes Carl her Royal Bodyguard, and puts on the Enchanted Crown of the Sepsis Whore while Mordecai is still warning her about it. It enters her in the line of succession of something called the Blood Sultanate, eight floors down. Carl punches a Bad Llama to death in the throat and pockets its meth. He still has no shoes, and the AI, reading out his new Smush skill, is breathing heavily about his feet.

beats.headline: Tally, the Hoarder, and the premiere
beats.text: The first safe room belongs to Tally, a Bopca Protector in a paper hat who cooks Carl the best murgh vindaloo of his life and special-orders salmon for Her Royal Highness. The screen over the counter counts crawlers, and it only goes down: ten million, then four. Carl throws goblin dynamite into a Scatterer nest and walks straight into his first boss, the Hoarder: fifteen feet of a woman in torn sweatpants who begs in Spanish and vomits roaches. He strangles her with a dog's leash and punches her until she dies, telling her he is sorry. The loot is spiked kneepads, not pants, and Donut asks whether there is a worst-dressed award. At the edge of the neighbourhood they find Rebecca W, stripped, shot once through a moth tattoo, an apple core in her box and her killer's name on the corpse. Carl decides he wants to find the man who did it. Then the first episode of Dungeon Crawler World airs over Tally's counter: Earth cut down to slums and dumps, forty minutes of people dying, and not one second of the Hoarder. The stairs begin to appear with a warning attached. Go down early and you wait in stasis, forgotten by the audience, until the floor collapses.

beats.headline: A meth war and a motorcycle
beats.text: A slime eats Carl's glove and his sleeve, and he has an idea: goblins build vehicles. The Goblin Pass tattoo turns their dots white, and Donut, charisma thirty-seven, reduces the shamanka to tears, sits in her lap and names her Rory. Two bags of llama meth buy the Goblin Copper Chopper, a steam bike with a fur-lined skull for a sidecar, and Donut helpfully tells the goblins where the meth came from. Every goblin in the workshop rolls out to war with the llamas. Carl and Donut strip the empty workshop, push a cart of black powder into the chieftain's chamber and blow it up. There were babies in there. The AI awards You Monster and War Criminal, lets Carl believe for twenty seconds that the babies are fine, and then tells him they are not. You might kill me, Carl decides, but you are not going to break me. Both get the Desperado Pass tattoo, which Donut calls a disqualifying mark. In the next safe room sits Frank Q, whose story is good and wrong in three places. He and his partner Maggie My pull their guns, freeze under the safe-room rules, and the Royal Court rides off leaving a rat corpse behind with lit dynamite in its inventory. A hundred miles east, a sign in red spray paint: stairs + people.

beats.headline: Meadow Lark, and a talk show
beats.text: The sign belongs to Meadow Lark, an elder-care home from Wenatchee that came down the stairs whole: the Andrews brothers, Brandon and Chris, who were the maintenance men; Yolanda Martinez, a nursing assistant with a bow; Imani, who has twelve crawler-killer skulls by her name and does not explain them; and Agatha, whom nobody can quite place. Behind them sit more than thirty residents who cannot fight, and the only stairs are guarded by a borough boss rolling around a spiral maze. Carl decides that if he is going to die, it may as well be for something. He and Donut grind, kill the Juicer (Donut opens his neck and breaks her own leg doing it), and come back with a war gauntlet that finally stops Carl breaking his knuckles. The fighters build a redoubt out of goblin tables and weight benches, Brandon calls it the Speedbump, and the Ball of Swine wedges itself on the roof until they stab it apart. Tusklings in tuxedos rain down. Carl kicks one until her health bar goes, and he may be crying. They push open the door at the bottom of the stairs and fall, not onto the next floor but into a production trailer. Lexis blocks out a segment, and Odette, a talk-show host in a crab suit, plays Carl his own catchphrase until he says it. Donut rolls over for the audience and promises they will kill with style. Off air Odette gives them the truth: loot is not always random, the Princess should stay a cat, and her own motive is money.
